The support ladder

When a student misses a question, Escalera finds out why.

Daniela missed an inference question. Each new try was a different question on the same skill, with more support. She got it right once the question was in Spanish, so the skill is there. Escalera sends her to practice the words she missed.

How a session works

One passage, one TEKS skill, every session.

Students move at their own pace. Every session ends with a short spoken or written answer.

1

Read

A short passage about something teens care about, written at the student's language level. Paragraphs are numbered, and every passage can be read aloud.

2

Answer

Questions on one TEKS skill, such as inference or theme, about the passage they just read.

3

Climb

After a miss, a new question on the same skill with more support: key words explained, then Spanish, then a worked example.

4

Respond

A short spoken or written answer in ACE format, with feedback in English and Spanish.

Mastery

Mastery means getting it right with no help.

Supports fade as a student improves. A skill counts as mastered when the student answers correctly with no supports at all. Time spent in the app does not count toward mastery.

Speaking and writing

Students speak and write every session.

Each session ends with a short answer in ACE format: Answer, Cite, Explain. Students type it or record it.

Escalera checks the answer against the rubric and gives feedback in English and Spanish. You can read every response and edit the feedback from your dashboard.

Did Maya make the right choice? Use one detail from the text.

I think Maya make the right choice. In paragraph 5, the text says she ties her apron tighter and takes the next order. This show she care about her dad.

  • Answer. You answered the question clearly.Respondiste la pregunta con claridad.
  • Cite. You used a good detail from paragraph 5.Usaste un buen detalle del párrafo 5.
  • Explain. Next step: tell why helping her dad matters more to Maya than the tryout.Siguiente paso: explica por qué ayudar a su papá es más importante para Maya que la prueba de fútbol.

For teachers

Know whether to teach the words or reteach the skill.

For every TEKS skill, your dashboard splits missed questions into two kinds.

  • Language gap means the student got it right once the words were explained or shown in Spanish.
  • Skill gap means the student needed the worked example to get it right.

Texas standards

Original texts for teens, tagged to Texas standards.

Every passage is short, original, and written for beginning English readers about things teenagers care about.

Every item is tagged to the English I TEKS and to the 2024 ELPS, which use five proficiency levels: Pre-Production, Beginning, Intermediate, High Intermediate, and Advanced. Speaking and writing tasks give students regular practice for TELPAS.
